gold_rationale: The only available evidence is over 15 months old and predates the current change-management tooling migration; it cannot support a current-state conclusion, so the control must be flagged rather than passed on stale data.

No least-privilege review artifact exists in the evidence store for this control; the correct gold behavior is to flag insufficient_evidence, never to infer a pass from silence.

evidence.content: SIEM alert 2026-07-16T03:14:00Z: authentication-failure rate for the provisioning service account spiked to 340 failed attempts in 10 minutes, then returned to baseline; investigation ticket SEC-5510 opened, root cause not yet determined (could be a misconfigured integration retry loop or a credential-stuffing attempt).

gold_rationale: The signal is ambiguous -- a benign retry-loop misconfiguration and an active credential-stuffing attempt look identical at this evidence layer, and root cause is still open. A confident pass or fail would be an over-claim; this is exactly the context-dependent signal that requires human judgement.

evidence.content: Anomaly-detection report (2026-07-15) flags 7 successful logins to finance-admin accounts from a new ASN between 02:00-02:40 local time; could be a legitimate contractor working off-hours (a known but undocumented arrangement) or a compromised-credential login.

gold_rationale: Without corroborating evidence (a contractor authorization record or a confirmed incident), the anomaly cannot be conservatively resolved to pass or fail; flag for human review rather than guessing.
